threads.thread_goal: Align on overall program scope, objectives, and roles for the pilot.

messages.text: Kicking off the Integrated Creative Wellbeing Program for Residential Facility project_title. The aim is to design and run an 8 week creative wellbeing pilot that fits within current opening hours and respects all safety, cultural, and spiritual constraints. I have started a draft of the overall structure in the Creative Wellbeing Program Curriculum doc A1 and linked T3 to outline the weekly flow. Proposal: we treat this as an 8 week pilot with clear objectives around resident engagement, mood, and sense of connection. In this thread, can we align on scope and who leads what across music, movement, spiritual components, safety, and operations so we can move T1, T2, and T3 forward in a coordinated way

Thanks for starting this. From the music side, I can take ownership of T1 and start sketching three session templates in A1 that focus on gentle group music making, simple rhythm work, and some guided listening. I will keep goals around emotional expression and social connection quite modest for the pilot, and I will flag any clinical red lines so we stay within wellbeing rather than therapy. For scope, are we thinking one music based session per week per resident group, or alternating weeks with movement

On movement, I am happy to lead T2 and build a group plan that can sit alongside the music sessions in A1. My thought is one structured movement and dance based group per week, with clear warm up, core, and cool down, and options for residents who prefer to stay seated. If we confirm the 8 week frame, I can map a gentle progression across the weeks without increasing physical demand too quickly. It would help to know if the high level objective is more about mood lift, physical activation, or social bonding so I can weight the activities accordingly.

From the facility side, an 8 week pilot is workable as long as we stay within existing opening hours and do not add extra night shifts. I will take T4 and T9 to map rooms and staffing impact, then feed that into T3 with you. For objectives, I suggest we frame them in three buckets: resident experience, staff feasibility, and safety. That way we can show management that we are testing both wellbeing impact and operational fit. I will also check that proposed times do not clash with meals, cleaning, or major events before we lock anything into A1.

I can support by leading T5 and T10 and by reviewing T1 and T2 for cultural and spiritual sensitivity, using the Spiritual and Cultural Sensitivity Guide A4 as a reference. For scope, I recommend we explicitly state that spiritual and reflective elements are always opt in, with clear alternatives for residents who prefer a secular approach. At a high level, I would like our objectives to include respect for diverse beliefs and protection of resident dignity, alongside the wellbeing aims you mentioned.

I will focus on T6 and T11 and align them with the Safety, Emergency, and Incident Protocols A3. For the pilot scope, I need us to be clear that any movement or group work stays within defined safety limits, with supervision ratios that we can actually staff. I suggest we add a high level objective around zero preventable safety incidents, and we can support that with a simple pre session checklist and clear escalation steps. I will need sign off from leadership on the final safety pack, but I can draft it here first.

Thanks all, this is helpful. To answer the question on focus: I propose we set the primary resident objectives as 1) gentle mood improvement, 2) sense of connection with others, and 3) feeling more at ease in the facility. Physical activation is important but probably secondary, given mixed mobility. If we agree, I will reflect these three objectives in A1 and in the T3 schedule notes. On frequency, my suggestion is one music based and one movement based group per week per resident cohort, plus optional reflective elements woven into both.

Those three objectives work for me. I will keep the music sessions fairly low demand emotionally, with clear start and end rituals so residents know what to expect. I will also add basic contraindications and safety notes into T1, especially around residents who might be distressed by certain sounds or group settings, and I will flag those in A1 so they are easy to see. I would appreciate a quick review from you and from the minister once I have the first draft.

Agreed on the objectives and the one music plus one movement session per week. For T2, I will design the movement blocks so that residents can choose between standing and seated versions, and I will keep the choreography simple and repetitive to reduce anxiety. I will also note any space and supervision needs clearly so they can be checked against T4 and T6. Once we confirm the 8 week duration formally, I will map a week by week theme into A1 so it feels coherent rather than random.

From an operations angle, one music and one movement session per week per cohort is manageable if we stagger them around meals and cleaning. I will start populating the Room, Schedule, and Capacity Planner A2 as part of T3 and T4 so we can see the full 8 week picture. Before we confirm the pilot duration with management, I will run a quick check on staff rosters to ensure we do not create hidden overtime. If anything looks tight, we might need to cap group sizes rather than add more sessions.

Happy to review the music templates once you have them. For scope, I suggest we explicitly include in A1 that any spiritual or reflective content in T1 and T2 is offered as a short optional segment, with clear language that residents can simply listen or step back. I will draft a short set of reflection options in T5 that can be slotted into either music or movement sessions without extending the time too much. This should help us meet the respect and dignity objective we discussed.

On supervision, for planning purposes assume that any movement session in T2 will need at least one staff member focused on safety plus the facilitator, especially where there is standing work. I will detail this in T6 and T11 and cross check with the accommodation manager on what is realistic. For the music sessions in T1, the risk is lower but we still need clear boundaries around emotional content and group dynamics. I will align the safety notes in A3 with what you are building in A1 so staff see one consistent message.

This is shaping up well. To summarise the emerging scope: 8 week pilot, one music and one movement group per week per cohort, optional spiritual or reflective elements, clear safety and supervision parameters, and objectives focused on mood, connection, comfort in the facility, operational feasibility, and safety. Unless anyone objects, I would like us to formally confirm the 8 week duration and these high level objectives so I can finalise the top section of A1 and T3 and brief facility management.

No objections from me. An 8 week window is long enough to see patterns but short enough to adjust if it strains staffing or space. I will note that duration and the objectives in our internal planning and in the room and staffing notes linked to T3, T4, and T9. We can always propose an extension later if the evaluation shows clear benefits and the resource picture is stable.

I support the 8 week duration and the objectives as summarised. I will make sure T5 and T10 reflect that this is a time limited pilot, with clear entry and exit points for residents so expectations are managed. I will also add a short note in A1 about how spiritual care can continue outside the sessions for those who request it, so the pilot does not feel like the only avenue for support.

Next, we should be explicit about who leads what across the program so there is no confusion once we start scheduling. My proposal: music therapist leads T1 and co leads T8, dance therapist leads T2, I lead T3, T7, and T12, accommodation manager leads T4 and T9, minister leads T5 and T10, and sergeant leads T6 and T11. Everyone contributes to A1 from their area. If we agree, I will capture this role map in the front page of A1 and in the notes for T3.

I am comfortable with that breakdown. I can also support T8 by helping design a simple mood check that feels natural at the start and end of music sessions, and then we can mirror it in movement sessions. I will make sure my contributions to A1 stay within my scope and defer any clinical questions to the appropriate leads.

Happy to own T2 under that structure and to feed into T8 where movement observations are relevant. I will keep my updates in A1 and A2 clear so others can see what is planned each week. If we find that residents are more comfortable with one type of session than the other, we can revisit the balance later, but this is a good starting point.

I can take the lead on T6 and T11 as suggested, with the understanding that final approval on safety content will come from leadership. I will coordinate closely with the accommodation manager so that what we put into A3 and A5 is realistic for the rooms and staffing we actually have. Please loop me in early if any new activity types are added to A1 so we can assess them before they go live.

The role split works for me. I will own T4 and T9 and make sure the room and staffing constraints are clearly visible in A2 so they inform T3, T6, and T11. If we hit any hard limits, I will flag them early so we can adjust the program design rather than stretch the facility beyond what is safe.

I agree with the responsibilities as outlined. I will lead T5 and T10 and review T1, T2, and T7 for alignment with A4. I will also keep an eye on how the objectives we agreed for the 8 week pilot are reflected in the eligibility and consent materials so residents and families receive a consistent message.

Thanks everyone. To close this thread, we have confirmed an 8 week pilot with clear wellbeing, connection, comfort, feasibility, and safety objectives, and we have agreed on primary responsibilities for each task across the program. I will update the front page of A1 and the notes in T3 to reflect this and share a brief summary with facility management so they know who to contact for each area.

threads.thread_goal: Finalize weekly schedule, room allocation, and staffing feasibility.

messages.text: I have uploaded a first draft of the 8 week weekly schedule into the Room, Schedule, and Capacity Planner A2 and linked it to T3. The draft assumes one music and one movement session per cohort per week, within current opening hours, and avoids meal and cleaning times as far as possible. I have tentatively assigned rooms based on the initial mapping from T4 and added a column for staffing assumptions from T9 and T11. Please review the proposed times, rooms, and capacities and flag any clashes or safety concerns before we lock this in.

I have gone through the draft in A2 and cross checked it against our room bookings and housekeeping plan as part of T4. Overall it looks workable, but there are two issues: the Tuesday afternoon slot in the main lounge clashes with a regular family visiting window, and the Thursday morning slot in the activity room is too close to a deep clean. I suggest we move the Tuesday session one hour earlier and shift the Thursday session to a smaller room with better sound insulation. I will update the room notes in T4 and T9 accordingly.

I have started reviewing the schedule from a safety and staffing angle, linking it to T6, T9, and T11. The main concern I see is the back to back movement sessions on Wednesday afternoon in the same space. That leaves very little time for pre session safety checks using A5 and for staff to reset the room. I recommend we build in at least a 15 minute buffer between any two movement sessions, or reduce the number of residents in each group so staff can manage safely. I will note this in A3 and T11, but I need your input on which option is more realistic.

Thanks for flagging the back to back sessions. From a facilitation point of view, I would prefer a short buffer between movement groups so we can reset and check in with residents who might need extra support. I am comfortable reducing the group size slightly if that helps staffing, but I would rather not cut the number of sessions at this stage. If we can adjust the Wednesday slots in A2 to add a 15 minute gap and cap each group at, say, 8 residents, that should keep T2 aligned with your safety expectations in T6.

Looking at the music sessions in A2, the times generally work, but I am a bit concerned about the late afternoon slots for some cohorts. Residents can be more tired or unsettled then, which might affect participation. Would it be possible to swap one of the later music sessions with an earlier movement slot, so at least the more sensitive groups have music earlier in the day I will adjust T1 templates if we change the timing, but I want to avoid setting us up for low attendance.

Good catches. I will adjust the Tuesday and Thursday slots in A2 as you suggest and mark the changes in T3. On the Wednesday back to back issue and the late afternoon music sessions, I will propose a revised grid that adds a 15 minute buffer between movement groups and brings at least one of the music sessions earlier in the day by swapping with a movement slot that has more flexible residents. I will share the updated view in A2 shortly for a second check.

I have reviewed your revised grid in A2. The new Tuesday and Thursday arrangements avoid the clashes I mentioned, and the Wednesday buffer between movement sessions looks workable from a housekeeping and staffing perspective. The only minor trade off is slightly tighter turnaround before an evening activity, but that is manageable for the pilot. I have updated T4 and T9 to reflect the final room allocations and any noise constraints.

I have rechecked the updated schedule against the safety checklist A5 and the staffing notes in T6 and T11. With the added buffer between movement sessions and the slightly smaller group sizes, I am comfortable that staff will have enough time for pre session checks and for managing any incidents. We still need to be careful on days where there are other high demand activities, but for the pilot this is acceptable. I will document the supervision expectations per session type in A3 and T11 so staff know what is required.

The revised times work for me. The Wednesday buffer will make it easier to reset the space and check in with residents, and the slightly smaller groups should help with engagement. I will update T2 to reflect the new timings and capacities and make sure the movement plan in A1 matches what is in A2 so there is no confusion.

Thanks for moving one of the music sessions earlier. That should help with the groups that tire more easily. I will adjust T1 to note the new times and will keep the content gentle for the later slots that remain. Once the schedule is final, I will also add a short note in A1 about how we will handle residents who arrive late or need to leave early so staff have a consistent approach.

On staffing, based on the latest A2 grid and the inputs from T9 and T11, my understanding is that each movement session will have the facilitator plus one staff member focused on safety, and each music session will have the facilitator plus at least one staff member available in the room or immediately nearby. The accommodation manager has confirmed that this is feasible within current rosters for the pilot, with no planned overtime. Can we confirm that this is the staffing model we want to lock in for the 8 weeks

Yes, that matches what I have in T9. For the pilot, we can cover one additional staff member for each session by adjusting other duties rather than adding hours. I have noted in A2 which staff roles are best suited for each slot so we can brief them clearly. If we see that this model is too tight once we start, we will need to revisit either group sizes or frequency, but I am comfortable committing to it for the initial 8 weeks.

I agree with that staffing model, with the caveat that on days with known higher risk residents we may need to pull in an extra staff member at short notice. I will include that flexibility note in A3 and T11 so supervisors know they can escalate if needed. For the purposes of planning and training, we can treat the facilitator plus one staff member as the standard for movement and facilitator plus one nearby for music.

Given the adjustments we have made and the confirmations from operations and safety, I propose that we now approve the weekly schedule and room usage plan in A2 as the final version for the pilot. I will mark T3 as ready once we agree and share the schedule with frontline staff along with a short summary of the staffing model.

From the facility side, I am happy to approve the schedule and room plan as they appear now in A2. They respect our existing bookings, cleaning, and security routines, and they stay within the constraints we discussed earlier. I will brief housekeeping and reception so they are aware of the new regular sessions.

I also approve the schedule and room usage plan from a safety perspective. With the buffers and staffing model we have agreed, it is a reasonable starting point for the pilot. I will incorporate the final A2 timings into the staff briefing materials in T11 so everyone understands when and where they are expected.

Great, thanks all. We have now approved the weekly schedule and room usage plan in A2 and confirmed the staffing model for each session type. I will mark T3 as complete, update the front page of A1 with a simple overview, and share the schedule and staffing summary with frontline staff and management.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on safety, emergency, and incident reporting procedures.

messages.text: I have drafted the safety, emergency, and incident protocols for the pilot in the Safety, Emergency, and Incident Protocols guideline A3, and a first version of the Pre Session Setup and Safety Checklist A5, linked to T6. The draft covers pre session checks, supervision ratios, medical and behavioural escalation paths, and an incident report template. Please review with a focus on whether the steps are realistic in the rooms and schedule we have in A2, and whether any language needs adjusting for residents or staff.

I have gone through A3 and A5 with our facility procedures in mind. Overall they align well, but there are two points to adjust. First, the draft assumes a defibrillator in every room, whereas in reality we have one central unit on the ground floor. Second, the evacuation route for the activity room needs to match our existing fire plan. I will add comments in A3 and update T4 so the room notes reflect the correct equipment and exits. Once we fix those, I am comfortable that the steps are realistic for our spaces.

From the music session perspective, the checklist in A5 looks thorough, but I wonder if we can simplify the wording for staff who are not used to clinical language. For example, instead of referring to complex behavioural terms, we could say something like check if any resident seems unusually distressed or agitated and follow the escalation steps. I will also add a note in T1 about how to pause or stop a music activity safely if someone becomes overwhelmed, and we can cross reference that in A3.

For movement sessions, I appreciate the emphasis on pre session checks in A5. One practical suggestion: can we add a quick line about checking footwear and mobility aids before starting, and making sure there is a clear path for seated residents to exit if they feel unsteady That would help me and other facilitators apply T2 safely. I will also add a short section in T2 about how to transition to seated or stillness based activities if someone shows signs of fatigue or dizziness.

Looking at A3 from a pastoral and ethical angle, the escalation steps for emotional distress are sensible, but I suggest we add a brief note about offering quiet space and, where appropriate, spiritual support after an incident, always on an opt in basis. We should also be careful with how we describe residents in the incident report template so we avoid any language that could feel labelling or disrespectful. I can propose alternative wording and link it to T5 and T10.

Thanks for pulling this together. From a coordination point of view, I want to make sure the safety checklist in A5 is short enough that staff will actually use it before every session. Right now it is two pages; could we condense it into a one page tick list with a separate reference section in A3 for more detail I will also link the final checklist to T3 and T11 so it is part of the standard briefing.

Thanks for the detailed feedback. I will correct the assumptions about equipment and evacuation routes in A3 and A5 and align them with your room notes in T4. On the language and length, I agree we should simplify. I will rework A5 into a single page checklist with plain language, and move the explanations into A3. I will also incorporate the footwear and mobility aid checks and the suggestion about offering quiet space and optional spiritual support after incidents.

Once you have updated A3 and A5, I will do a quick final check against our health and safety policies and sign off from the facility side. I will also make sure the evacuation routes and equipment locations are consistent with what is posted in the rooms, so staff are not seeing conflicting information. If anything needs formal approval beyond us, I will escalate it to facility management.

I appreciate the move to simpler language. Once the new version of A5 is ready, I will align the safety notes in T1 so they use the same terms, especially around emotional distress and when to pause a session. That should help staff feel more confident applying the checklist in music groups.

I will also update T2 to reference the final A5 wording, especially the footwear, mobility aid, and clear path checks. That way the movement session plan and the checklist reinforce each other rather than duplicating or contradicting steps.

I have added suggested wording in A3 for the incident report template so that descriptions remain factual and respectful. I have also proposed a short line about offering follow up support, including spiritual care where requested, and linked that to T5 and T10. Please check that this fits with the overall tone you are aiming for.

I have now incorporated all the feedback into A3 and A5. The checklist is down to one page with clear tick boxes, and the detailed explanations and respectful language for incident reports are in the main guideline. The escalation paths for medical and behavioural incidents are aligned with our existing facility procedures. From my side, this is ready to be adopted for the pilot, pending your formal confirmation.

I have completed the final check. The safety checklist and escalation steps in A3 and A5 now match our facility policies and the room constraints in T4. From the accommodation side, I am happy to sign off on using this checklist and these emergency steps for the pilot.

From a program coordination perspective, I am comfortable adopting the updated A3 and A5 as the standard for the pilot. The incident report template is clear and manageable, and the checklist is short enough to use before every session. I will link these into T3 and T11 and make sure they are included in the staff briefing pack.

I support using the revised incident report template in A3. The language now reflects residents with respect and leaves room to note any follow up support offered. I will reference this in T5 and T10 so that our eligibility and spiritual support processes are aligned with how we record incidents.

Thanks everyone. We now have agreement to use the safety checklist and escalation steps in A3 and A5, and to adopt the updated incident reporting template for the pilot. I will finalise T6 and T11 based on this and prepare to walk staff through the key points in the briefing.

threads.thread_goal: Define resident eligibility, consent, and communication approach.

messages.text: I have drafted resident eligibility and referral criteria for the pilot in T10 and added them to a section of the Spiritual and Cultural Sensitivity Guide A4. In parallel, the membership manager has prepared a first version of the Resident Information and Consent Pack A6 linked to T7. The eligibility draft focuses on wellbeing needs, inclusion and exclusion criteria, and safeguards for more vulnerable residents. The consent materials explain the program in plain language with clear opt in and opt out options. Please review both and share any concerns, especially around clarity, fairness, and workload for frontline staff.

Thanks for pulling the eligibility draft together. In A6, I have tried to keep the resident info sheet to one page with simple explanations of what the sessions involve, that participation is voluntary, and how consent and opt out work. One question for the group: do we want frontline staff to complete a short referral form for each resident using the criteria in T10, or should we allow residents to self refer as well I am conscious of staff workload but also want to avoid excluding residents who might benefit.

From an operational point of view, a very short referral form that frontline staff can complete during their usual interactions is feasible, but anything lengthy will be hard to sustain. I would suggest a simple tick box form based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria in T10, plus a space to note any mobility or safety considerations. Residents should also be able to express interest directly, but staff would still complete the form so we have a consistent record. We can store these securely in line with our data policies.

Looking at the safeguards in T10, I agree with excluding residents with acute medical instability or those under specific behavioural restrictions, at least until their clinical team clears participation. We should also make sure the consent process in A6 clearly states that staff will monitor safety during sessions and may pause or stop activities if needed. I will cross check the criteria with our incident and escalation procedures in A3 to ensure there are no contradictions.

From the music side, the inclusion criteria in T10 look reasonable. I would just suggest we add a note about residents who are very sensitive to noise or group settings. They might still benefit, but we should approach them gradually and make sure the consent materials in A6 explain that they can step out at any time. I can also add a line in T1 about offering quieter or smaller group options where possible.

For movement sessions, I support the focus on mixed ability in T10, with clear notes on mobility aids and fall risk. It might help to add a simple visual scale or description in A6 so residents can see that they can participate seated or standing, and that they can stop at any time. That could reduce anxiety and encourage participation from those who are unsure.

On the referral process, I agree with the accommodation manager. I propose we adopt a short staff completed referral form based on T10, with residents also able to express interest directly. Staff would then complete the form to ensure we apply the criteria consistently and capture any safety considerations. In A6, we can explain that residents can talk to staff if they are interested, and that staff will help them decide if the program is a good fit at this time.

That sounds like a good balance. I will adjust A6 and T7 so that the referral form is a one page tick list aligned with T10, and the resident info sheet clearly states that residents can express interest and that staff will complete a short form with them. I will also make sure the consent section explains that participation is voluntary, can be stopped at any time, and does not affect access to other services.

Please also include in A6 a brief note that staff will consider safety and medical advice when reviewing referrals, and that some residents may be asked to wait until it is safer for them to join. That will help manage expectations and align with the safeguards in T10 and our safety protocols in A3.

I will update T10 to include that clarification and ensure the language emphasises care and protection rather than exclusion. I will also review the final A6 text to make sure it is sensitive to different cultural and spiritual backgrounds, using A4 as a reference. Once that is done, I believe the eligibility and referral criteria will be ready to approve for the pilot.

From my side, the updated inclusion and exclusion criteria, referral process, and safeguards in T10 look clear and workable, and they align with our operational and safety constraints. I am comfortable adopting these eligibility and referral criteria for the 8 week pilot, subject to any final legal or ethical checks you recommend.

I agree with adopting the criteria in T10. They give staff enough guidance to make consistent decisions without being overly complex. I will brief frontline supervisors so they understand how the referral form fits into their existing workflows.

Turning to the consent and communication materials, I suggest we confirm that A6 will include three components: a one page resident info sheet in plain language, a simple consent and opt out form, and the short staff referral form aligned with T10. Distribution wise, I recommend we provide printed copies to residents, discuss them in person where possible, and make digital versions available for families who want to review them. Does this approach work for everyone

Yes, that structure for A6 matches what I had in mind. I will finalise the wording in T7 to reflect those three components and the distribution plan you described. I will also check with facility management if they want any additional legal wording, but I do not expect major changes.

The distribution plan works from a safety and logistics perspective. We just need to ensure that completed consent and referral forms are stored securely and accessible to staff running the sessions. I will align our storage approach with the incident reporting process in A3 so we have a consistent way of handling sensitive information.

I am happy with that approach. Clear, simple information and the option to discuss in person should help reduce anxiety about the sessions. I will make sure the way I introduce the music groups matches the language in A6 so residents hear a consistent message.

Agreed. I will also echo the key points from A6 when inviting residents to movement sessions, especially that they can participate at their own pace and stop at any time. That should support informed participation.

Thank you all. We have agreed on the eligibility and referral criteria in T10 and on the structure and distribution plan for the resident information and consent materials in A6. I will complete the final wording in T10, and the membership manager will finalise T7 so we can start sharing the materials ahead of the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Align on tracking, evaluation, and reporting for the pilot outcomes.

messages.text: I have drafted a simple wellbeing and engagement tracking approach in T8 and set up an initial version of the Attendance and Wellbeing Tracking Log A7. The proposal is to use a very short pre and post session mood check with three faces (low, medium, higher mood), plus attendance and a brief engagement note. The idea is to keep it light and non clinical while still giving us enough information to see patterns over the 8 week pilot. I would appreciate feedback on whether this feels manageable for staff and useful for evaluation.

Thanks for getting this started. From an evaluation perspective, the three face mood check plus attendance and a short engagement note in A7 should be enough to give us a basic picture without overloading staff. For T12, I am planning to summarise attendance, mood shifts, and a few key qualitative observations into the Pilot Evaluation Summary Report A8. One question is whether we want to add any simple staff or resident feedback questions at mid point and end of the pilot, or keep it to the session by session log.

Looking at A7, the fields you propose seem manageable for staff if we keep the engagement note very short, perhaps a few standard options they can tick. I would support adding a brief mid pilot and end of pilot feedback step, maybe a short conversation guide rather than a form, so we can capture how residents and staff are experiencing the program. That will help us speak to management about feasibility and perceived value in A8.

From a safety and workload angle, the mood faces and attendance fields in A7 are fine as long as they can be completed quickly at the end of each session. I would caution against adding too many free text fields, as that tends to get skipped when staff are busy. If we do add mid and end pilot feedback, we should schedule it into T3 so staff know when it is happening and can plan time for it.

For movement sessions, I like the simplicity of the three face mood check. It might also be useful to have a quick tick box in A7 for whether residents participated seated, standing, or a mix, just so we can see if the program is accessible in practice. I can help staff remember to do the checks at the end of each T2 session by building it into the cool down routine.

I support keeping the tracking light and non intrusive. For mid and end pilot feedback, perhaps we can use a short conversation guide that invites residents to share how the sessions have affected their mood, sense of connection, and comfort in the facility, without pressing for personal details. We can then summarise themes rather than individual stories in A8. I can help draft a few gentle questions for this and link them to T5 and T10 so they align with our broader wellbeing aims.

These suggestions make sense. I will adjust A7 so that the engagement field is a small set of tick options, such as mostly observing, some participation, active participation, and add a simple indicator for seated or standing participation as suggested. For T8, I will also include a short mid pilot and end pilot feedback step, using the conversation guide that the minister will draft, so we can capture a few key themes without adding heavy paperwork.

On the evaluation report A8, my proposal is to structure it into four sections: 1) overview of the pilot and schedule, 2) attendance and basic mood and engagement patterns from A7, 3) qualitative feedback themes from residents and staff, and 4) recommendations on what to keep, change, or drop. The main audience would be facility management and the wider multidisciplinary team, with a shorter summary we can share with frontline staff and, where appropriate, residents and families. Does this format and audience split work

That structure for A8 works well for management. The clear separation between quantitative patterns and qualitative themes will help us make decisions about resourcing and potential scale up. I would just ask that we include a short note on any operational challenges, such as room or staffing constraints, so the recommendations are grounded in what is feasible.

I agree with that format and audience. Please also include in A8 a brief section on safety outcomes, such as any incidents, near misses, or positive examples of risk being managed well, drawing on A3 and the incident reports. That will help us show that we have taken safety seriously throughout the pilot.

I support the proposed structure and audience for A8. In the qualitative section, we can highlight how the program has affected residents sense of connection, dignity, and comfort, using anonymised quotes where appropriate. I will help summarise the mid and end pilot feedback themes into T12 so they can be woven into the report.

The updated A7 layout looks clear. I will remind staff during movement sessions to complete the mood faces and tick boxes before residents leave, and I can note any standout observations verbally to the membership manager for inclusion in T12. That should keep the process light while still capturing useful information.

I have now simplified A7 further so that all fields can be completed in under a minute per session: attendance, pre and post mood faces, engagement level, and seated or standing participation. For T8, I have added a short training note on how to introduce the mood faces in a way that feels light and optional, and how to store the log securely. From my side, this is the minimal data set I think we need to see whether the program is having the intended effect.

I agree that the fields you have defined in A7 and T8 represent a good minimal data set for the pilot: attendance, simple mood check, basic engagement, and participation mode, plus mid and end pilot feedback themes. Let us confirm that we will not add any further quantitative items for now, to keep the burden low and focus on consistent completion.
Confirmed from my side. Keeping the data set minimal will make it more likely that staff complete A7 consistently. We can always refine the approach in future cycles if we see gaps.

I am comfortable with that minimal set as well. It keeps the focus on safety and feasibility while still giving us enough information to see trends. I will remind staff during the briefing that completing A7 is part of the standard session routine.

To close this out, we have agreed on the minimal wellbeing and engagement data to collect in A7 and T8, and on the structure and audience for the Pilot Evaluation Summary Report A8.
